terra.problem: The explanation is flat and repetitive: it restates the cracked ground without adding much of Papa Dorin's voice.
The passage does not say whether the doe is following anyone.
Saying barren means nothing is growing goes beyond the stated lack of pasture.
The prayer confesses sin, but the passage does not identify its speaker as the people.
The passage does not identify the people as the prayer's speaker. The prayer also includes another request, not to be forsaken.
The passage does not identify the people as the speaker of the prayer.
Saying they do not dodge their sin attributes the confession to the people; the passage does not identify the prayer's speaker.
The explanation says the people make the confession, but the passage does not identify the prayer's speaker.
Saying they make the statement presents the people as speakers, though the passage does not identify the prayer's speaker.
The prayer says the LORD is among them; it does not say He is not above them or that they speak to Him face to face.
The passage does not identify the prayer's speaker or say the LORD is not on His way.
The text does not say the request is spoken loudly.
The passage does not identify the people as the ones speaking the prayer.
The verse says the people may offer sacrifices; it does not say the offerings are brought.
The prophets' quoted promise rules out sword and famine and promises peace; it does not say there will be no disaster of any kind.
The passage does not say the prophets never ask for anything, or that Jeremiah brings up their message because it contains no call to change.
